subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool + burst policy / SLA coordination (OrbitalAI)
messages:
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@orbitalai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@orbitalai.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool + Bursting for OrbitalAI

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited to move forward. To align expectations for our Dedicated deployment, we want to confirm a few items before the formal SOW:

- Target steady-state throughput: ~120 reqs/min at p95 latency under 2s for our 2k-token models.
- Expected peak bursting window: up to 3x steady-state for 10-minute bursts during daily retraining and batch re-annotations.
- Regional preference: primary in us-west, fallback to us-east for capacity spikes.

Can Redwood confirm recommended pool size, autoscale policy parameters, and any networking pre-reqs? Sam and Alex will own internal approvals; we need a short mutual action plan so procurement can schedule the signature.

Attached a quick spreadsheet with our expected traffic profile (capacity_estimates.xlsx). Also looping in Alex for infra questions.

Best,
Sam Rivera
Head of ML Platform
OrbitalAI

Attachments: capacity_estimates.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 16:10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool + Bursting for OrbitalAI

Sam — thanks for the clear profile and for sharing the spreadsheet. Quick confirmation on our side before Ben and Marissa add technical and onboarding specifics:

- We can provision a dedicated GPU pool in us-west as the primary region with automatic cross-region fallback to us-east.
- For 2k-token models, our initial recommendation is a pool sized for ~150 concurrent tokens/streams (we'll convert this to vGPU counts after Ben reviews).
- Bursting: Redwood Dedicated supports short-term burst to an account-level burst reserve (configurable). We typically recommend a burst ceiling of 2.5–3x steady-state and a burn-rate alarm at 70% so teams can choose to throttle non-critical workloads.

Ben will propose concrete vGPU counts and autoscale thresholds, and Marissa will own the implementation timeline and handoff checklist. If possible, can you confirm the procurement timeline so we can align the canary window?

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben: technical sizing + network/security ask (by EOD Monday).
2) Marissa: 3-week implementation plan + MMS (mutual action plan) draft (by Tuesday).
3) Sam/Orbital: procurement target date and PO/contract owner.

I'll follow up with a brief canary/fallback playbook after Ben's sizing.

— Soojin
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 09:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool + Bursting for OrbitalAI

On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 4:10 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the clear profile and for sharing the spreadsheet. Quick confirmation on our side before Ben and Marissa add technical and onboarding specifics:

Thanks — dug into the attached traffic profile. A few technical notes and a proposed config (high-level):

1) Baseline pool sizing
- For 2k-token models with your p95 target, we estimate baseline of 4x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (conservative) or 6x for improved headroom if you want <2s p95 under some variance.
- We'll present both a "cost-optimized" (4x) and "latency-optimized" (6x) option in the SOW.

2) Autoscale + burst policy (proposed)
- Scaling unit: vGPU instance (we map to your workload via continuous batching).
- Target CPU utilization-equivalent for autoscale: keep token-service utilization at 55%–65% to allow rapid autoscale without thrashing.
- Scale-up policy: add 1 vGPU when sustained utilization >65% for 45s (immediately apply prefix-cache warmstart to new nodes).
- Scale-down policy: remove 1 vGPU when utilization <35% for 180s and no in-flight long-run requests.
- Burst reserve: allocate a burst pool of 3x baseline capped at 10 min per burst window; integrate a protective fallback that demotes non-critical workloads (batch re-annotation) to queued mode.

3) Networking & security (pre-reqs)
- VPC peering/S2S VPN: allow outbound to Redwood control plane IPs and open egress to our regional inference endpoints.
- Private key rotation: provide KMS ARN for vault integration; we support HSM-backed KMS on request.
- Audit logs: we'll enable per-request tracing for the canary window (30 days retention by default unless enterprise retention is requested).

4) Canary plan and SLA implications
- Canary window: 72-hour canary with canary traffic representing ~20% of steady-state.
- SLA: once Dedicated is live and canary passes, we can add a 99.5% uptime SLA for the provisioned pool in the SOW (depends on committed reserved capacity).

Attachments referenced: network_diagram.png (simple diagram of peering + routes). I attached a quick spreadsheet with vGPU mapping and cost delta for 4x vs 6x (capacity_estimates.xlsx).

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: network_diagram.png, capacity_estimates.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool + Bursting for OrbitalAI — Implementation checklist and next actions

Hi Sam — putting a short mutual action plan (MAP) and checklist here to keep approvals tight and get provisioning scheduled. I created a draft SOW (Orbital_SOW_v1.pdf) with both sizing options; attaching here for review.

Mutual Action Plan (high level)
- Week 0 (this week): Finalize SOW option (cost vs latency). Orbital to confirm preferred sizing and PO/contract owner.
- Week 1: Legal/Procurement review and signature; Redwood prepares infra tickets and pre-provisioning checklist.
- Week 2: Network setup (VPC peering, KMS details), credentials exchange, and canary cluster boot.
- Week 3: Canary (72h) + smoke tests, RBAC and key rotation verification.
- Week 4: Cutover to production pool and post-cutover monitoring runbook handoff.

Action items for Orbital
- Confirm sizing option (reply-all with "cost" or "latency").
- Provide procurement timeline and PO contact (name + email).
- Share KMS ARN or let us know if you need HSM (we'll add to SOW).

Action items for Redwood
- Deliver final SOW with selected sizing and SLA addendum.
- Runbook and regression eval suite for canary.
- Provide pre-provisioning checklist and network diagram.

Please review the attached SOW and if that looks OK, confirm which sizing path you prefer so we can lock lead times for us-west GPUs. If procurement can sign within 10 business days we can start network setup early next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min sync if you want to walk the SOW line-by-line.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
